html:
An earthquake of magnitude about 8.7 that struck the eastern Himalaya on 15 August 1950, centred in the Mishmi Hills near the border of Assam in India and Tibet. It is one of the strongest earthquakes on land ever recorded.

It killed several thousand people in Assam and Tibet. The shaking set off huge landslides that blocked rivers in the hills. When these natural dams burst, days or weeks later, floods swept down the valleys. The Brahmaputra and its tributaries carried so much sand and silt that their beds rose, and floods in Assam grew worse for years afterwards. Some river courses shifted for good.

It came on India's third Independence Day and the year Chinese forces entered Tibet. Together with the 1934 Bihar and Nepal earthquake, it showed how dangerous the Himalayan front is. The same event seen from the Tibetan side is described under Assam and Tibet earthquake.
sum: An earthquake of magnitude about 8.7 that struck the eastern Himalaya on 15 August 1950, centred in the Mishmi Hills near the border of Assam in India and Tibet. It is one of the strongest earthquakes on land ever recorded.
